headline: DMP collects data on landlords and tenants to boost city security
summary: The Citizen Information Management System (CIMS) has already registered over 5 million citizens and 3.6 million families in Dhaka.
details: The Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) is operating the Citizen Information Management System (CIMS) to ensure citizen security and maintain law and order in the capital.
Through this system, basic information of landlords, tenants, and mess members living in Dhaka is being registered, stored, and updated.
Launched in 2016 at Ramna Police Station, the software-based system was expanded to all stations in 2017, followed by the launch of a mobile app in 2019.
Currently, the CIMS database contains registrations for approximately 3,673,238 families and stores information for over 5 million citizens.
DMP states that accurate and updated information helps make beat policing more effective, prevents crime, aids in investigations, and helps identify missing persons or suspects.
Citizens can obtain CIMS forms from any police station or post in Dhaka, fill them out and submit them to the respective station, keeping a photocopy for their records.
Landlords can use CIMS to verify the identity of tenants, reducing the risk of harboring criminals or fraudsters, while tenants gain easier access to legal aid and identity verification.
The DMP has urged all landlords, tenants, and mess members in the capital to complete their registration to help build a safe, smart, and crime-free Dhaka.
caption:
Over 5 million Dhaka residents are already registered in the DMP's security database. Is your information updated?

The Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) is operating the Citizen Information Management System (CIMS) to ensure citizen security and maintain law and order in the capital.

Through this system, basic information of landlords, tenants, and mess members living in Dhaka is being registered, stored, and updated.

Launched in 2016 at Ramna Police Station, the software-based system was expanded to all stations in 2017, followed by the launch of a mobile app in 2019.

Currently, the CIMS database contains registrations for approximately 3,673,238 families and stores information for over 5 million citizens.

DMP states that accurate and updated information helps make beat policing more effective, prevents crime, aids in investigations, and helps identify missing persons or suspects.

Citizens can obtain CIMS forms from any police station or post in Dhaka, fill them out and submit them to the respective station, keeping a photocopy for their records.

Landlords can use CIMS to verify the identity of tenants, reducing the risk of harboring criminals or fraudsters, while tenants gain easier access to legal aid and identity verification.

The DMP has urged all landlords, tenants, and mess members in the capital to complete their registration to help build a safe, smart, and crime-free Dhaka.

headline_marked: Ex-state minister [[Zunaid Ahmed Palak seeks more time with lawyers]] in court
headline: Ex-state minister Zunaid Ahmed Palak seeks more time with lawyers in court
summary: Facing 98 cases, the former minister claims health issues and limited access to legal counsel during a hearing in Dhaka.
details: Former State Minister Zunaid Ahmed Palak requested more time to consult with his lawyers during a hearing at the Dhaka Metropolitan Sessions Judge's Court on Sunday.
Palak told the court he is unwell and has a neck injury, which led doctors to advise against wearing a helmet. He also noted that he has been in remand for 99 days and faces 98 different cases.

He specifically requested the court to allow him at least three hours of consultation with his lawyers twice every two weeks, citing that he currently only gets 30 minutes with his family every 15 days.

The hearing was part of a case regarding the death of truck driver Md. Hossain, who was shot dead during the July protests. Former PM Sheikh Hasina and 33 others, including Palak, are accused in this case.

While appearing in court, Palak was seen flashing 'V' signs to his supporters, an action the public prosecutor described as an attempt to create 'public sentiment' and as 'indecent' for an accused person.
Over 100 supporters gathered at the court to see him, and police subsequently detained four individuals from the crowd during the process of returning him to the prison van.
